concept_html:
Hugging Face transformers loads a pretrained model and its tokenizer by name. In transformers 5.22:

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
    name, num_labels=3, id2label=id2label, label2id=label2id)
batch = tokenizer(texts, padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=128, return_tensors="pt")
out = model(**batch, labels=labels)       # out.loss, out.logits
  • The load report. Loading prints a table. classifier.weight and classifier.bias marked MISSING are the new head, initialised at random. That is expected. A missing encoder key is not (lesson B26-L1).
  • The batch. input_ids holds token IDs, attention_mask holds 1 for real tokens and 0 for padding, and BERT-style models add token_type_ids. Pass them all with **batch.
  • The loss follows the labels. The model sets config.problem_type from the first labels it sees. Integer labels give cross-entropy. Float labels with num_labels above 1 give a multi-label loss, sigmoid per class. num_labels=1 gives mean squared error. One-hot float labels silently train a multi-label model.
  • Train mode. from_pretrained returns the model in eval mode. Call model.train() before training, so dropout is on.

For LoRA, peft 0.21 wraps the model:

config = LoraConfig(task_type=TaskType.SEQ_CLS, r=8, lora_alpha=16, target_modules=["query", "value"])
model = get_peft_model(model, config)
model.print_trainable_parameters()

task_type=TaskType.SEQ_CLS keeps the new classifier trainable. Leave it out and the classifier stays frozen at its random start. On a small BERT, that trained 4,096 values instead of 4,291, and the missing 195 were the whole head. Target names depend on the architecture. BERT calls its projections query and value, and a name the model lacks raises NoMatchingPeftModuleError.

lines: import torch
from peft import LoraConfig, TaskType, get_peft_model
from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification
def build_classifier(name: str, labels: list[str], r: int = 8) -> torch.nn.Module:
"""A pretrained encoder with a new head and LoRA on queries and values.
Args:
name: Hugging Face model name or local folder.
labels: Class names, in ID order.
r: LoRA rank.
Returns:
The peft model in train mode.
"""
id2label = dict(enumerate(labels))
label2id = {label: i for i, label in id2label.items()}
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
name, num_labels=len(labels), id2label=id2label, label2id=label2id
)
config = LoraConfig(
task_type=TaskType.SEQ_CLS, r=r, lora_alpha=2 * r, target_modules=["query", "value"]
)
peft_model = get_peft_model(model, config)
peft_model.train()
return peft_model
def training_loss(model: torch.nn.Module, batch: dict[str, torch.Tensor], labels: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
"""Cross-entropy loss for one batch. labels must be integer class IDs."""
if labels.dtype != torch.long:
raise TypeError(f"labels must be torch.long class IDs, got {labels.dtype}")
return model(**batch, labels=labels).loss

  • Use the distinct labels, sorted, so IDs do not depend on row order.
  • Return (id2label, label2id), with IDs from 0.

exercises.solution:
def label_maps(labels: list[str]) -> tuple[dict[int, str], dict[str, int]]:
    """ID-to-label and label-to-ID maps for a classifier head.

    Args:
        labels: One label per row, repeats allowed.

    Returns:
        (id2label, label2id), numbering the sorted distinct labels from 0.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If there are fewer than 2 distinct labels.
    """
    names = sorted(set(labels))
    if len(names) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"need at least 2 distinct labels, got {names}")
    id2label = dict(enumerate(names))
    return id2label, {name: i for i, name in id2label.items()}

exercises.prompt_html:
Write pad_batch(seqs, pad_id, max_length) -> tuple[list[list[int]], list[list[int]]], what padding=True, truncation=True does to token IDs.

  • Cut each sequence to at most max_length IDs.
  • Pad every sequence at the end with pad_id to the longest length after cutting.
  • Return (input_ids, attention_mask), with mask 1 for real IDs and 0 for padding.
  • Raise ValueError if seqs is empty or max_length is below 1.
exercises.solution:
def pad_batch(
    seqs: list[list[int]], pad_id: int, max_length: int
) -> tuple[list[list[int]], list[list[int]]]:
    """Truncate and right-pad token IDs, with an attention mask.

    Args:
        seqs: Token IDs per text.
        pad_id: ID used for padding.
        max_length: Longest allowed sequence.

    Returns:
        (input_ids, attention_mask), all rows of equal length.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If seqs is empty or max_length is below 1.
    """
    if not seqs or max_length < 1:
        raise ValueError("need at least one sequence and max_length of at least 1")
    cut = [s[:max_length] for s in seqs]
    width = max(len(s) for s in cut)
    ids = [s + [pad_id] * (width - len(s)) for s in cut]
    mask = [[1] * len(s) + [0] * (width - len(s)) for s in cut]
    return ids, mask

title: Fine-tuning a text classifier with Hugging Face
why_html: A team fine-tuned a LoRA classifier for complaint categories and got accuracy no better than always predicting the largest category. The training loss fell a little and stalled. Their LoraConfig had no task_type, so the randomly initialised head never trained, and the adapters could only bend the encoder towards a random projection. Adding task_type=TaskType.SEQ_CLS fixed it on the next run.
